title: 江村即事
titleEn: A Moment in a River Village
author: 司空曙
intro: A fisherman comes home too sleepy to tie up his boat — and doesn’t care. Four lines about the freedom of a life with nothing to lose.
analysis: “即事”就是“眼前的事”。诗写一个渔人：钓完鱼回来，连船都懒得拴，月亮已经落下，正好倒头就睡。第三、四句是他心里的想法：就算夜里起风把船吹走了，又能漂到哪儿去呢？最多停在长着芦花的浅水边罢了。一般人怕船被吹走，他却一点不担心，这份满不在乎写出了江村生活的安宁，也写出了一种不计较得失、随遇而安的心态。诗里用了“纵然……只在……”的转折，先假设最坏的情况，再轻轻一笑说“没关系”，读起来很轻松。
analysisEn: 即事 means “what is in front of me right now”. The poem follows a fisherman home after a day on the river. He is so ready for bed that he doesn’t even tie up his boat; the moon has already set, and it’s the perfect time to sleep. The last two lines show what goes through his mind: even if the wind blows all night and carries the boat off, where could it go? At most it will drift into the shallows by the reed flowers. Most people would worry about losing their boat; he simply shrugs. That carelessness tells us how peaceful the village is — and also shows an attitude Chinese poets admired: not clinging to gain and loss, being content wherever you end up. Notice the structure 纵然……只在…… (“even if… still only…”): the poet imagines the worst that could happen, then smiles and says it hardly matters. That light touch is what makes this little poem so easy to love.
background: Sikong Shu (c. 720–c. 790) was one of the “Ten Talents of the Dali Era”, a group of mid-Tang poets. He held minor posts and lived through hard times after the An Lushan Rebellion; his poems are known for plain, quiet scenes.
pronunciation: 系船 xì（拴，不读口语“系鞋带”的 jì）；堪 kān；纵然 zòng。

lines.py: diào bà guī lái bù xì chuán
lines.lit: Done fishing, I come home and don’t tie up the boat;
lines.en: Home from fishing, I don’t bother tying up the boat —

lines.py: jiāng cūn yuè luò zhèng kān mián
lines.lit: in the river village the moon has set — just right for sleep.
lines.en: the moon is down, the village asleep, and so am I.

lines.py: zòng rán yī yè fēng chuī qù
lines.lit: Even if all night the wind blows it away,
lines.en: And if the wind should carry it off in the night,

lines.py: zhǐ zài lú huā qiǎn shuǐ biān
lines.lit: it will only be by the reed flowers at the shallow water’s edge.
lines.en: it will only drift to the reeds in the shallows.

words.en: on the scene; writing about what is in front of you
words.note: 古诗题常用语，现代汉语不说。
现代汉语说“完”，如“钓完”；“罢了”“作罢”还用。
“系船”读 xì；口语“系鞋带”读 jì。
古义；现代汉语“不堪”“难堪”还用。
现代汉语说“睡”；“失眠”“冬眠”还用。
书面语，现代汉语也用，口语说“就算”。

words.en: reed flowers; the fluffy white tops of reeds

imagery.name: 船
imagery.zh: 不系的船象征渔人自由自在、无牵无挂的生活。
imagery.en: The untied boat stands for the fisherman’s free, carefree life — nothing holds him, and nothing worries him.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 月落点明时间已到深夜，江村一片安睡。
imagery.en: The setting moon tells us it is late night and the whole village is asleep.

imagery.name: 水
imagery.zh: 芦花浅水是船最多能漂去的地方，代表江村的安稳和小小的天地。
imagery.en: The reedy shallows are the farthest the boat can drift — a small, safe world where nothing is ever really lost.
